name: No gag on criticism
standard: No non-disparagement clause, or only a short, mutual one that never covers safety, ethics or legal concerns. Never for life.
why: Staff and ex-staff are often the only people who can tell the public a lab is cutting corners.

name: Equity is never hostage
standard: Vested equity and pay can't be cancelled, clawed back or blocked from sale because someone spoke out.
why: Threatening vested equity turns a contract into a gag.

name: Protected disclosures carved out
standard: The contract says in plain words that nothing in it stops reporting to regulators, government, law enforcement or a lawyer.
why: Mirrors legal protections like California SB 53 and the UK's PIDA, so staff don't have to guess.

name: Whistleblowing policy is public
standard: The full speak-up / whistleblowing policy is published, not just a code of conduct.
why: Lets outsiders check the process actually exists and is any good.

name: Safe internal channel
standard: An anonymous internal channel, a real anti-retaliation policy, and someone independent of leadership who sees reports.
why: Most concerns should be fixable inside the company, if people trust the route.

name: Secrets means secrets
standard: Confidentiality covers genuine secrets (model weights, code, unreleased research, customer data), not opinions about how the company behaves.
why: Protects what labs legitimately need to protect, and nothing more.

name: No secret NDAs
standard: Staff can say they signed an agreement and what kind it is.
why: A gag you can't admit exists is the worst kind.
